analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction about repeated overdraft fees totalling £180 and describes financial hardship (skipping meals), meeting the CH-1 definition of financial loss and material distress.
analysis.summary: A student customer complains about repeated unarranged overdraft fees: 12 fees between August and October 2026, totalling £180. The customer says the fees use up their student loan each time it arrives, and that they have been skipping meals to make money last. They ask the bank to stop the fees and refund some of them. These are clear signs of financial difficulty and a risk to wellbeing, which requires a fee review under FEE-4 and a referral to Vulnerable Customer Support under VUL-4. The customer has not yet been asked about support needs. They prefer contact by email. A statement for August to October 2026 is on file.

timeline.event: Handler noted account, fee count, email contact preference; support needs not yet asked

analysis.severity_reason: The loss is £180, which on its own would be Medium. However, the customer reports skipping meals because of the fees, so a vulnerable customer is at risk of harm, which makes this High under CH-6.

vulnerability.suggested_support: Ask the customer sensitively, by their preferred method (email), whether they need any support. Refer the case to Vulnerable Customer Support. Consider signposting to free debt and money advice and to a student account or arranged overdraft option. Offer reasonable adjustments such as a named contact and more time to respond.

analysis.routing_reason: The customer shows a vulnerability indicator (low or erratic income, as a student relying on loan instalments) together with financial difficulty and a risk to wellbeing (skipping meals). VUL-4 and FEE-4 therefore require a referral to Vulnerable Customer Support. The fee review itself can stay with the complaints handler.

policy_citations.quote: Where a customer shows signs of financial difficulty, fees charged in the last 6 months should be reviewed and refunded where they have added to the difficulty. The case must also be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team under policy VUL.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer shows financial difficulty, so the overdraft fees from the last 6 months should be reviewed and the case referred to Vulnerable Customer Support.

policy_citations.quote: Cases with a vulnerability indicator *and* any of: financial difficulty, risk to health or wellbeing, suspected financial abuse, or bereavement must be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: There is a resilience indicator together with both financial difficulty and a risk to wellbeing (skipping meals), so referral is required.

policy_citations.quote: *resilience* (low or erratic income, problem debt, financial difficulty)
policy_citations.how_it_applies: As a student, the customer's income comes in loan instalments, and they are in financial difficulty.

policy_citations.quote: a vulnerable customer at risk of harm
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Skipping meals indicates a risk of harm, which supports High severity.
The disputed fees are unarranged overdraft fees on a current account, so the Fees and Charges Refund Policy applies.

policy_citations.quote: If in doubt, record it as a possible vulnerability and ask the customer, sensitively, whether they need any support.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer has not yet been asked about support needs.

evidence.quote: I've been skipping meals to make it last.
I keep getting charged overdraft fees. It's been £180 in three months.
Please can you stop the fees and refund some of them.
Every time my loan comes in, the fees eat it.

handover.complaint_summary: A student customer has been charged 12 unarranged overdraft fees totalling £180 between August and October 2026. They say the fees consume their student loan instalments and that they are skipping meals to make money last. They want the fees stopped and some of them refunded. Complaint received 2026-10-29; final response due 2026-12-24; status On track (45 days left).
handover.desired_outcome: "Please can you stop the fees and refund some of them."
actions_taken: Account and fee history reviewed: 12 unarranged overdraft fees, August to October 2026, totalling £180
handover.vulnerability_assessment: Indicators found: resilience (student relying on loan income, in financial difficulty) and a possible health or wellbeing risk (skipping meals). Possible capability factor (likely limited experience with financial products). The customer has not yet been asked about support needs.
handover.contact_preference: Email ([EMAIL_1]). No reasonable adjustments recorded yet.
open_questions: What support does the customer need, and do they consent to the vulnerability indicators being recorded?
Is the account on a suitable tariff for a student, and is an arranged overdraft or student account available?
Should fees from the last 6 months be reviewed under FEE-4, including any charged before August?
Is the customer in other financial difficulty, such as other debts?

other_gaps: Fee history earlier than August, within the 6-month FEE-4 review window, has not been checked
Account type and tariff are not stated
Whether the customer has received any previous discretionary fee refunds is not recorded
analysis.suggested_next_step: Email the customer to acknowledge the complaint, ask sensitively about any support needs and seek consent to record them. Refer the case to Vulnerable Customer Support within 2 business days. A handler should then review the overdraft fees from the last 6 months under FEE-4 and decide any refund.
